title: Control Flow: If/Else
description: Learn how to make decisions in your programs using conditional statements. Control which code runs based on conditions.
objectives: Write if statements for simple conditions
Use else and else if for alternative paths
Use the ternary operator for simple conditionals

sections.title: Making Decisions
sections.content:
Programs often need to make decisions - do one thing if a condition is true, something else if it's false.

The **if statement** is the fundamental building block for decision-making in programming.

sections.title: If Statement Syntax
sections.explanation: BPL's if syntax is similar to C, Java, and JavaScript - condition in parentheses, code in braces.

sections.title: Basic If Statement
sections.expectedOutput:
You are an adult!
It's hot outside!
You passed!

lineExplanations.7: If age is 18 or more, execute the code block.
lineExplanations.13: If temperature is greater than 30, print the message.
lineExplanations.20: The code inside braces only runs if score >= 60.

sections.title: If-Else: Two Paths

lineExplanations.7: number % 2 == 0 checks if the remainder when divided by 2 is 0 (even).
lineExplanations.9: The 'else' block runs when the condition is false.
lineExplanations.16: This check determines if the balance is positive or negative.

sections.title: Else-If: Multiple Conditions

lineExplanations.7-17: Conditions are checked in order. First true one wins.
lineExplanations.9: 'else if' adds another condition to check.
lineExplanations.15: Final 'else' is the default if nothing else matches.
lineExplanations.22-34: Multiple else-if creates a chain of conditions.

sections.title: Nested If Statements
sections.expectedOutput:
Old enough to drive
Has a license
Fully legal to drive!

lineExplanations.9: First check: is the person old enough?
lineExplanations.12: Second check (nested): do they have a license?
lineExplanations.15: Third check (deeper nested): do they have insurance?

sections.title: Combining Conditions
sections.expectedOutput:
Entry allowed (age and ID check passed)
Regular price
Qualifies for assistance program

lineExplanations.9: && means both conditions must be true.
lineExplanations.14: || means at least one condition must be true.
lineExplanations.24: Use parentheses to group conditions for clarity.

sections.title: Ternary Operator (Shorthand If)
sections.expectedOutput:
Status: Pass
Category: Minor
Max of 10 and 20 is 20

lineExplanations.7: The ternary operator is a one-line if-else.
lineExplanations.18: Great for selecting between two values based on a condition.

sections.title: Practice: Number Classifier
sections.instructions:
Write a program that:
1. Takes a number (use -7)
2. Prints whether it's positive, negative, or zero
3. If positive, also print if it's even or odd
sections.hint: Use nested if statements - first check the sign, then check even/odd inside the positive branch.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **if (condition)** executes code when condition is true

✅ **else** provides alternative when condition is false

✅ **else if** chains multiple conditions

✅ Conditions can be combined with **&&** (AND) and **||** (OR)

✅ **Ternary operator** `?:` is shorthand for simple if-else

✅ Always use **braces { }** even for single statements (good practice)

questions.question: What prints when x = 5? if (x > 10) { print A } else { print B }
questions.explanation: 5 is not greater than 10, so the else branch executes, printing B.

questions.question: What is true && false || true?
questions.explanation: && has higher precedence. (true && false) = false. false || true = true.

questions.question: What does 'x > 5 ? 10 : 20' return when x = 3?
questions.explanation: 3 is not greater than 5, so the 'else' part (20) is returned.
